references.text: The priest was not to make himself unclean by any dead person, even for his father or mother. The Nazirite had similar restrictions.
Ezekiel describes the priests' rules about uncleanness from the dead, which resemble the Nazirite's obligations.
The priests were forbidden to make themselves unclean through contact with the dead, except for close relatives. The Nazirite had even stricter requirements.
If someone died suddenly near a Nazirite, his consecrated head became unclean, and he had to cleanse himself.
The introduction to the Nazirite vow explaining dedication to the Lord.
Jesus calls a man to follow him and lets the dead bury their own dead, showing a higher dedication than even family obligations.
Jesus teaches that following him takes priority over burying one's father, a principle similar to the Nazirite's separation.
